answer: The finality of attestations only counts when the attestator is established, so a fresh cluster of aliases cannot push any transaction to finality until it has spent many epochs proving honesty. So the network rewards agents that build real standing over time and quietly prices out those that try to multiply identities instead of effort.. This is durable because the trusted grader set only grows through bootstrap capacity, preventing a sudden takeover by a large new flock. Consider a juniper as the anchor of the cost.
